key_step: Recast both sides via J = int_0^1 sqrt(1-y^2) dy (quarter circle) and solve for I
justification: Several routine area evaluations (parabola area, semicircle symmetry, polynomial integral) chained, with one linear equation at the end and options to match; the only slightly non-routine move is reading dx- and dy-integrals as the same area. Like 2023-P2-Q1 (L2: routine chain with a small twist) and below 2021-P2-Q12 (L4).

key_step: Separable kernel: f=(A+1)sin+B cos with A=int f, B=int t f; solve 2 linear equations using odd/even
justification: Two constants, two parity-based linear equations and one final integral; a standard coaching pattern with no real insight but numerical format (no options). Comparable to 2023-P2-Q1 (L2, integral equation to a simple solve).

key_step: Limits from max/min of the Mobius expression; split max{f,x} at x=9/5; divide polynomial and integrate
justification: Four stages (derivative test, limits, crossing point, integral with polynomial division and logarithm) with exact arithmetic in a numerical answer, so one slip is fatal; no single hard idea. Above 2026-P2-Q3 (L2, SCQ DE with quartic finish) because of the numerical format and extra stage.

key_step: Partial fractions into two logs, then solve ln-equation for b
justification: Routine partial fractions and two standard log integrals followed by an algebraic equation solved by recognising 49/50 = (1/2)(7/5)^2. No insight, moderate algebra. Similar demand to 2023-P2-Q9 (L2, linear DE then optimisation).

key_step: King property: P(x)+P(pi-x)=pi^3/2 collapses the integrand
justification: One familiar move (king property) plus algebra to see that the cubic sums to a constant, then a standard arctan integral; numerical format nudges it above the simplest king-property anchor 2026-P2-Q4 (L1).

key_step: Divide by x^2, t=x+2/x, then int dt/(t sqrt(t^2-4)) = (1/2) sec^-1(t/2)
justification: The substitution x+c/x is a recognition trick students may or may not have drilled, followed by a less common sec^-1 antiderivative and an improper endpoint; numerical, so no options to check. Easier than the L4 anchor 2025-P2-Q16 (king-type substitution with tan^-1) but harder than the plain L1 king property 2026-P2-Q4.

key_step: Make the denominator sin60+sin2x and use sum-to-product so the integrand splits into cosec and sec
justification: Needs the multiplier sqrt3/2 insight, a sum-to-product and angle-addition decoding of the numerator, then csc/sec integrals converted to the tan form of the options; long but options help. Alternate u=sinx+cosx is more standard. Comparable to 2024-P1-Q1 (L2) with extra trig manipulation.

key_step: By parts on sec^2x sin^-2022 x: leftover integral cancels, giving I = tan x / sin^2022 x
justification: One recognition (by-parts with cancellation) and then routine evaluation of closed-form values with large exponents; options make it checkable. Like 2023-P2-Q1 (L2).

key_step: f is a period-2 triangle wave; reduce [-10,10] to one period and integrate by parts
justification: Decode a [x]-defined piecewise function, notice periodicity, shift the second half, then by parts; three ideas linked but each standard. Easier than 2021-P2-Q19 (L4, greatest-integer breakpoints numerical) because it is option-based and only one period is needed.

key_step: Multiply by e^{2x} and split; u=e^x gives sqrt2 tan^-1; two points determine e^alpha
justification: Non-obvious algebraic rewrite, an arctan integral with a constant that is easy to get wrong, use of two conditions and tan addition; SCQ so some checking possible. Close to 2026-P2-Q3 (L2) in DE chain but with a longer integration and trig finishing.
